brief.t: Week ending Oct 15: corn commitments 22,193 '000 MT for 2026/27 (9,544 shipped, 12,648 outstanding) = **28% of USDA's 3,300 m bu** export forecast, vs a 5-yr norm of 38% by week 7. (Export sales usually capture 95% of USDA's census-basis exports — median of the last 5 seasons — so USDA's 3,300 m bu is taken as 79,430 '000 MT on the export-sales basis.) Commitments are -34% vs a year ago. Three ways to project the season from here (USDA units): if this week's 28% is the usual share of the final, about 2,443; if the rest of the season adds what it added in the last 5 seasons, about **2,449** (range 1,987–3,101); if it repeats last season's finish, 3,101. Middle estimate **2,449 m bu** (-26% vs USDA) — early-season sales are a weak guide to the final number for this crop, so treat this as a direction, not a forecast.

To reach USDA's 3,300 m bu, the US needs 58,351 '000 MT more net sales (including the usual 1,113 carried into next season) — 1,297/week for 45 weeks. Over the same weeks the last 5 seasons sold 857/week on average (range 582–1,162; last season 1,162); that total was reached in 0 of the last 5 seasons and 0 of 10 — **sales look not achieved in any recent season**. Recent pace: 989/week over the last 4 weeks (5-yr avg for these weeks 1,340). Shipments need 1,553/week vs 1,223/week shipped over the rest of the season on average (best of 5: 1,667); reached in 1 of 5 seasons — shipping capacity looks a stretch. Shipped so far 12% of target (norm 9%).
Net sales 1,527 vs 1,122 the week before (+36%), -46% vs the same week last year and -19% vs the 5-yr average. Shipments 780 vs 1,363 (-43%), -45% vs last year, -10% vs the 5-yr average.
Net sales 6,755 (-41% y/y, -11% vs 5-yr avg); shipments 9,544 (+2% y/y); outstanding sales 12,648 (-48% y/y); next-season sales on the books 402.

Shipments usually concentrate in the next three months for Canada (31% of its season), Guatemala (26% of its season), Spain (26% of its season).

Export outlook vs USDA: **below USDA's 3,300 m bu**. Pointing lower: sales pace, destination buying. Pointing higher: competitor exports. Export outlook vs USDA: **balanced around USDA's 175 m bu**. Pointing lower: destination buying. Pointing higher: competitor exports. Middle projection 176 m bu (+1%); the sales USDA's number needs were reached in 3 of the last 5 seasons (8 of 10). Already well bought: South Korea. Less competition usually shows up later in the season, once rival origins run short — watch whether US sales accelerate into the new year before reading the slow start as lost demand.

Week ending Oct 15: cotton commitments 5,655 '000 bales for 2026/27 (1,943 shipped, 3,712 outstanding) = **47% of USDA's 12.30 m bales** export forecast, vs a 5-yr norm of 54% by week 11. (Export sales usually capture 97% of USDA's census-basis exports — median of the last 5 seasons — so USDA's 12.30 m bales is taken as 11,925 '000 bales on the export-sales basis.) Commitments are +16% vs a year ago. Three ways to project the season from here (USDA units): if this week's 47% is the usual share of the final, about 10.71; if the rest of the season adds what it added in the last 5 seasons, about **11.41** (range 9.56–12.81); if it repeats last season's finish, 12.81. Middle estimate **11.41 m bales** (-7% vs USDA) — below USDA; a cut is possible unless sales pick up. The %-of-USDA comparison understates the pace when USDA's target is larger than in past seasons; the second method does not depend on the target.

To reach USDA's 12.30 m bales, the US needs 7,279 '000 bales more net sales (including the usual 1,009 carried into next season) — 178/week for 41 weeks. Over the same weeks the last 5 seasons sold 164/week on average (range 138–185; last season 181); that total was reached in 2 of the last 5 seasons and 6 of 10 — **sales look a stretch**. Recent pace: 182/week over the last 4 weeks (5-yr avg for these weeks 170). Shipments need 243/week vs 245/week shipped over the rest of the season on average (best of 5: 279); reached in 3 of 5 seasons — shipping capacity looks achievable. Shipped so far 16% of target (norm 15%).
Net sales 202 vs 157 the week before (+28%), +12% vs the same week last year and +9% vs the 5-yr average. Shipments 204 vs 151 (+35%), +24% vs last year, +61% vs the 5-yr average.
Net sales 1,598 (-16% y/y, -13% vs 5-yr avg); shipments 1,943 (+24% y/y); outstanding sales 3,712 (+12% y/y); next-season sales on the books 574.
